Ascended Heroes card list and printing guide

2026-11-05 · Updated 2026-11-10

Browse the card list and price samples

This Ascended Heroes guide separates the official English card numbering from the dated Card AI price samples. Match the complete number, language and finish before using a sample. Check the observation date for each price, and use the current catalog record when available; a missing price is not zero.

Find the set.Match the card. · Find your Pokémon card. Check its value. · Read a price.Understand the comparison.

One card number can have several finishes

Card AI identifies the expansion as ME: Ascended Heroes, code ASC. Its catalog can hold several records for one printed number, including different patterns or finishes. Those records are not extra checklist numbers. Keep the pattern visible when you compare prices, and confirm the artwork and language before choosing a holding.

The table retains all official numbered entries even when the snapshot has no matching record. Team Rocket's Energy 217/217 is one such entry in this snapshot. It remains in the checklist with no substitute price.

Missing prices stay missing. Code cards, boxes, packs and unnumbered promos are not part of this numbered checklist. These reference values are not offers or guaranteed sale prices. Check the official card gallery against the artwork on your copy.

How to compare an Ascended Heroes card

Start with the collector number, then compare the card's name and image with the official gallery. Inspect the foil or pattern on the copy you own. A plain finish and an Energy Symbol Pattern must not silently share a reference price.

In the Pokemon card scanner, a photo produces candidates for review. Confirm the record, language and finish, then choose a raw condition or enter the grade on an existing slab. Use the website checklist and text lookup for reference. Photo scanning and saving personal holdings take place in the Card AI app.

Prices and checklist completion answer different questions

Owning every numbered card and owning every finish are different collection goals. This page shows numbered cards and available catalog price samples without calculating your personal completion percentage. The digital card binder explains the saved fields used to distinguish copies, while the collection tracker follows confirmed holdings and their available values.

Compare the smaller numbered lists for Chaos Rising and Phantasmal Flames. For a specific Charizard printing, see the Mega Charizard X ex guide; a familiar name in another expansion is not the same card.
